A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SynthWorlds framework and datasets. Their main text and Appendices A–D, including equations, figures, tables, and prompts, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-hop QA and navigation experiments with GPT-5-mini and Gemini-2.0-Flash, plus human validation of the generated data in Appendix B.5.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds evaluations of gpt-oss and Kimi-K2 models in Figures 4–5 and Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: The graph sampling, entity renaming, timestamp perturbation, parallel document generation, and task construction procedures remain unchanged, including their detailed specifications and prompts in Appendices A–B. New examples explain existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Wikidata-derived parallel corpora, 1,200 QA questions across six motifs, and 1,000 navigation pairs across five difficulty buckets. Mathematics and code generation appear only as possible future applications in v3.

E2.justification: Tables 4–5 expand beyond v1's GPT-5-mini and Gemini-2.0-Flash comparisons: gpt-oss-20b and gpt-oss-120b participate in both tasks, while Kimi-K2-Instruct and Kimi-K2-Thinking join navigation. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator set; the QA and navigation baseline procedures remain the same.

E3.justification: v3 adds comparisons across 20B/120B model sizes and instruct/thinking variants within the existing evaluation design. The task counts, metrics, ten-document reading-comprehension setting, ten-step IRCoT limit, and thirty-step navigation cap are retained.

E4.justification: Figures 4–5 extend the existing analyses of knowledge access and task difficulty to additional models. The new gpt-oss comparisons expose cases where iterative retrieval reduces the knowledge gap while worsening absolute performance. Human validation, corpus diagnostics, and the external-entity reasoning-trace analysis are retained.

E5.justification: v1 already reports confidence intervals and error bars. Appendix C in v3 newly specifies 5,000 bootstrap resamples and percentile bounds for F1, and Wilson intervals for navigation success. This adds statistical reporting detail without establishing additional independent experimental runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds eight QA rows and eight navigation rows, together with difficulty-specific results. For example, gpt-oss-20b has RM F1 of 41.0 with one-step RAG but 30.7 with IRCoT. Figure 4 also revises Gemini IRCoT motif-level curves, although the original GPT-5-mini and Gemini aggregate entries in Tables 4–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The knowledge-advantage equations, graph definitions, sampling formula, and construction constraints are retained. The added discussion of motif difficulty supplies intuitive explanations rather than new formal definitions, proofs, or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, three principal contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about controlled parallel worlds, disentangling factual knowledge from reasoning, and persistent knowledge advantages. Additional model evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 attributes gpt-oss's IRCoT performance losses to difficulty following the prompt format, qualifying the benefits of iterative knowledge integration. Section 6 also expands applicability discussion to graphs extracted from text and possible mathematics/code adaptations, emphasizing graph quality and domain-dependent renaming.

D1.justification: New Section 8 adds experimental code/data access information, and Appendix C specifies statistical implementation details. However, Section 6 now names GPT-5-mini for indexing while Appendix C retains model-matched NER/OpenIE instructions, leaving that setting ambiguous. Existing construction prompts, costs, and shared inference details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for gpt-oss, both Kimi variants, GoLLIE, and a generative information-extraction survey. These support the expanded experiments and discussion of constructing knowledge graphs from text; the central related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds explanatory examples for renaming and difficulty, separates insights from future extensions, introduces a reproducibility section, and makes local wording corrections. The overall narrative and most appendix prose remain intact; the header changes to the ICLR 2026 publication designation.

P2.justification: The principal result displays are substantially reworked: Figure 4 expands from two to four models and removes its motif thumbnails, while Figure 5 becomes a three-row comparison covering six models. Tables 4–5 expand and are reorganized, including grouped headers in Table 4 and separate placement of Table 5.

improvement.justification: The broader model comparisons strengthen evidence for persistent knowledge advantages and reveal an IRCoT failure mode absent from v1's two-model evaluation. Clearer explanations and documented interval construction improve transparency. These gains are tempered by incomplete settings for the added models and the indexing-description ambiguity between Section 6 and Appendix C.
